name: The Cruciform Depot
description:
Buried beneath the intersection of four decommissioned freight rail lines in the old industrial southwest, the Cruciform Depot is a subterranean interchange station that Axiom Industries mothballed in 2147 and formally abandoned in 2161. Its four converging tunnel arms stretch outward under the city like compass points, each arm now claimed by a different faction for storage, transit, or purposes less easily categorized. The central hub chamber—forty meters across and vaulted in cracked ferrocrete—serves as a neutral trading floor that none of the four arm-factions are willing to let any of the others control outright.

The Depot exists in a legal gray zone: Axiom's abandonment filing was never properly recorded with the city infrastructure authority, meaning no one has clear title and Ferrogate Security lacks a clean jurisdictional hook to enter without triggering a corporate arbitration process. This technicality is the Depot's most valuable asset, cited daily by the lawyers, fixers, and mid-tier operators who use the space precisely because it is, for practical purposes, unwatchable.

sights: Four tunnel mouths lit in different colored biolamp strips—each arm-faction's chosen marker—converging on the dim central hub
Stacked Carrion Logistics containers repurposed as offices and meeting rooms along the hub's curved walls
A cracked mosaic floor from the station's original 2090s construction, partially buried under decades of grime and cable runs
sounds: The low subsonic vibration of surface freight traffic passing overhead, felt more than heard
Overlapping negotiations in half a dozen languages echoing off the ferrocrete vault
The occasional distant clang from one of the tunnel arms, source always unclear
smells: Old machine oil and mineral groundwater seeping through the walls
Street food carried in by vendors who set up along the hub perimeter during peak hours
Ozone from a cluster of overworked portable Diaspora relay nodes near the south tunnel mouth
atmosphere.feel: The Depot has the atmosphere of a place that knows it is borrowed time—everyone present is conducting business they would prefer not to conduct elsewhere, and the politeness is professional rather than warm. The four-way balance of power creates a studied neutrality that can collapse without warning if any one faction overreaches.

demographics: A rotating population of Tier 2 and Tier 3 operators, fixers, and mid-level corponation contractors; no permanent residents, though a handful of individuals appear to have been living in the container offices for months.
economy: Neutral-ground deal brokerage, data escrow services, untaxed goods transit between the four tunnel arms, and a small but consistent trade in Axiom Industries legacy infrastructure documents that surface periodically from the sealed lower maintenance levels.
power_structure: An uneasy four-way standoff between the arm-factions—reportedly backed by Palladian Group, Sterling-Nakamura, an independent operator collective, and an entity whose affiliation no one will confirm—with hub neutrality enforced by the collective threat of mutually assured commercial disruption.
dangers: Factional agreements collapse periodically, turning hub negotiations into armed standoffs in an enclosed underground space with limited exits
The sealed lower maintenance levels have reported anomalous activity consistent with an E.L.F. presence, and at least two retrieval teams sent to investigate have not returned
Axiom Industries has recently retained a Palladian Group legal team to revisit the abandonment filing, threatening to establish clear title and end the Depot's jurisdictional immunity
opportunities: The neutral hub is one of the few spaces in the megacity where representatives of rival corponations can meet without either party triggering surveillance flags
Axiom-era infrastructure documents from the lower levels reportedly include original BCI network routing maps predating current Diaspora architecture—priceless to the right buyer
The independent operator collective controlling the west tunnel arm is quietly seeking new members with specific technical skills, offering access and protection in exchange
story_hooks: A data package placed in escrow at the Depot six months ago by a now-dead Sterling-Nakamura mid-manager has reached its release date. Three separate parties have arrived to claim it simultaneously, each presenting documentation that appears legitimate, and the hub's neutrality depends on someone resolving the dispute before weapons come out.

Sounds from the sealed lower maintenance levels have changed character over the past two weeks—less random, more rhythmic. One of the tunnel arm factions is paying for a discrete investigation, but they are insisting on a team with no corponation affiliations, which in 2200 is a nearly impossible qualification to meet.
frequented_by: Mid-tier fixers and brokers maintaining corponation-neutral reputations for cross-faction deal facilitation
Tier 3 contraband logistics operators using the tunnel arms as a switching point away from surface surveillance
Corponation legal and intelligence staff conducting meetings that cannot appear in their employer's activity logs
Arcturus Defense Solutions contractors whose presence in the south tunnel arm is never officially acknowledged
